lines.l: And the drums did go with a rock-a-tot and the pipes to loudly play
Fare thee well, Polly, me dear, I must be going away
All night they tossed and tumbled till daylight did appear
The soldier rose, caught us close, said, fare you well, me dear
For the drums, they are a-sounding and the pipes to sweetly play
If it weren't for that, dear Polly, then along with you would stay
And the drums did go with a rock-a-tot and the pipes to loudly play
Fare thee well, Polly, me dear, I must be going away
Oh, come, you gentleman soldier, won't you marry me?
Oh, no, me dearest Polly, such things never can be
For I've a wife already, a children I have three
Two wives are all out in the army, but one's too many for me
And the drums that go on the run, the tatt, and the fives that know they play
Fare thee well, Polly, me dear, I must be going away
If anyone comes according to you, you can treat them to a glass
If anyone comes according to you, you can say you're a country lass
You don't have to tell them that ever you play this joke
That you were drilled in the sentry box dropped up when the soldiers told
And the drums they'd go with a rat-a-tat-tat and the fights they'd loudly play
Fare thee well, Polly, my dear, I must be going away
Oh, come, you gentleman soldier, why didn't you tell me so
My parents will be angry when this they come to know
And when nine long months are coming past, that poor girl she brought shame
She had a little militia boy and she didn't know his name
And the drums that go up, the rat-a-tat-tat, and the fives that loudly play
Fairly well, Polly, my dear, I must be going away
Last night as I slept
